Comms and calendar

Comms and calendar

Draft templated email, preview recipients, send via outbox, and manage calendar invites.

Where comms live

Open Admin → Comms. Templates define subject and body with program fields. Sending is a staged flow — Audience → Message → Review → Send — so the recipient set and rendered bodies are always reviewed before anything queues. Send enqueues outbox work for asynchronous drain — the request path does not call the email provider directly. The delivery log shows the template, recipients, and local send times (row ids live in tooltips), and the ICS panel uses human-readable copy with the raw invites collapsed.

Draft and preview

Choose a template, set audience filters, and run preview. Inspect missing fields before any send. Fix person or session data when required tokens are blank. Calendar invites (ICS with stable UID/SEQUENCE) are generated when the template and event data support them; on the hosted demo, email carries no attachments and speakers download the .ics from the portal instead.

  1. Open Admin → Comms and select a template.
  2. Configure audience and event context.
  3. Run preview and read recipients, bodies, and missingFields.
  4. Repair data or template tokens until missing fields are acceptable.
  5. Only then send with the appropriate role and confirmation.

Scopes and CLI

comms:draft allows preview automation. comms:send is default-deny on new API keys and required for send. Agents should draft and show humans a preview before any key with send is used in production.

speakerops comms templates --event <eventId> --json
speakerops comms draft --template <templateId> --preview --json
speakerops comms send --preview-id <previewId> --json

Delivery backends

Local and many dev paths use sandbox provider behavior. Demo uses Cloudflare Email Sending, which delivers no attachments — calendar .ics files reach speakers as a portal download. Other environments may use Resend (attachment-capable) when EMAIL_PROVIDER=resend and secrets are set. Operators should know which provider the current host uses before debugging inbox issues.

WARNING. Never put raw API keys or magic links into template bodies. Prefer product tokens and portal links that require auth.

Where this lives in the app

  • /admin/comms

Open these routes on your demo or local host while you follow the steps above.
